_readme: CANONICAL ROSTER of Hermes event-bus subscribers. Single source of truth.
Read events/roster.py first -- it defines the schema, the validation rules,
and why this is a JSON data file rather than a Python constant.
Consumers (add yourself here if you add another):
- events/gateway_integration.py startup()  -- asserts the REGISTERED set
equals the 'live' set here and emits AGENT_ERROR on any mismatch. This
is the mechanism that makes drift self-announcing: the check runs
against real subscriber objects, so no id is ever guessed or parsed.
- hermes_cli/events_doctor.py               -- derives its required-cursor
list from entries flagged "core": true.
- scripts/event_bus_retention.py (+ the profiles/main mirror)
-- reads this file WITHOUT importing the package (stdlib json, absolute
path) to classify subscriber_cursors rows. It is a --no-agent cron and
must stay import-free of agent-src.
WHEN YOU ADD A SUBSCRIBER: register it in startup() and add a "live" entry
here. Forgetting the entry is not silent -- the next gateway boot emits an
AGENT_ERROR naming it.
WHEN YOU RETIRE A SUBSCRIBER: comment out its register() call, flip its
entry to "retired", set "since" and "cursor_frozen_at_rowid" to the rowid
its cursor stopped at (read it from subscriber_cursors). NEVER delete the
entry while its cursor row survives: the entry is what keeps
--prune-cursor refusing it and keeps the nightly unknown-cursor warning
quiet. A retired entry whose cursor later MOVES is reported nightly.

subscribers.note: Seeds its cursor at 0 for a gap-free forensic trail (SEED_CURSOR_AT_CONSTRUCTION=False).

Registered UNCONDITIONALLY (inside a try/except around the jobflow_dispatch import) so its cursor advances and lag_report() covers it; merely INERT unless HERMES_JOBFLOW_EVENT_DISPATCH is set -- which it currently is ('on'). Absent from the retention script's roster until 2026-08-23, which made the nightly sweep WARN about a live subscriber whose cursor advances every few minutes and tell the operator to prune it. Pruning a live cursor is not cosmetic: the subscriber would resume from a reset position. That drift is the reason this file exists.

Registered like any other subscriber (so startup_all() builds its IntentApplier and shutdown_all()/lag_report() cover it) but driven by a DEDICATED thread and SKIPPED in the serial poll loop. Its cursor is type-filtered and legitimately advances only when tracker intents arrive -- do NOT add a generic frozen-cursor alarm on the strength of it.

v1-era shadow-copy of mailbox_message events to the Agent Comms topic. The v2 cutover collapsed Agent Comms and Digests into one scribe_daily topic, which TelegramNotifier already routes mailbox_message to -- keeping this registered duplicated every delivery. Registration commented out at events/gateway_integration.py. No cursor row survives (null above means 'no cursor row expected'); if one ever appears, the nightly sweep reports it. events_doctor kept it in its required list until 2026-07-12, producing a permanent false FAIL on every run -- the third-copy drift this roster removes.

Retired under routing v3 P2 (one-event-one-message): its narrated mailbox_message NOTIFICATION copies duplicated the typed delivery of the same 7 event types (interview/offer landed in THREE topics per event). Typed events are canonical; plain-language bodies live in events/formatting.py. Registration commented out; class + tests kept for history. The retention script listed it as LIVE until 2026-08-23 -- harmless to the cursor logic, but it told every reader the gateway still ran it.

Never registered in startup() -- it was a direct bus.subscribe() consumer running outside the gateway, which is why the register()-vs-roster check cannot see it and why this file, not startup(), is the roster. Retired as dead weight: no producer emits devflow.run_*, and the session-mirror bridge superseded the intended producer on 2026-07-21. Cron paused + watchdog cadence removed. Do not prune; do not re-add to the watchdog's EXPECTED_CADENCE_SECONDS.
